newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian insurer cracks Thai market, eyes China.
newsitem.headline: Australian insurer cracks Thai market, eyes China.

text.p: Australian insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd on Wednesday won a licence to operate in Thailand, meeting a key Asian objective and leaving the group focused on its top priority, China.

"We've now secured a licence in Thailand. Certainly the key one we're still pursuing is a licence in China...," managing director National Mutual international Geoff Webb told Reuters. "China is our number one market for new entry."
Australian Prime Minister John Howard is expected to help National Mutual's cause during a visit to Beijing this week.
"There are many factors that influence whether the company is going to get a licence or not. Certainly having the strong support of your home government is very important," Webb said.
"The fact that the prime minister will raise these issues is a demonstrable indication of the government's support," he added.
Since 1989, National Mutual, owned 51 percent by French insurance giant Axa SA, has been vying for a slice of the Chinese insurance market, potentially the world's largest.
"There is certainly (in China) a viable market for life insurance and that will only continue to grow," Webb said.

In recent years the firm has forged links with Chinese insurer China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd, donated HK$10 million (US$1.3 million) to set up a China education fund and last September launched a US$500 million China investment fund.
Now it wants to double the number of its representative offices in China to six.

Webb said National Mutual's managing director, Geoff Tomlinson, would be voicing the group's aspirations to Chinese authorities personally as part of an 18-strong business delegation travelling with Prime Minister Howard on his visit.
"Certainly access for Australian insurers I'm sure will be on the agenda," says Webb.

Tomlinson will not be the only one championing the cause of Australian life offices in China in the coming days, with Colonial Ltd managing director Peter Smedley another member of the prime minister's business entourage.
National Mutual's A$11 million (US$8.6 million) investment in the Thai venture marries the group with the country's second largest commercial bank, Krung Thai Bank Plc.
The two will hold 45 percent each of the joint venture. Thai businessman Chinavais Sarasas, who has links to the local insurance market, owns the rest.
The new Krungthai AXA Life business will also receive distribution assistance from the Thai bank.
